delectable

dih-LEK-tuh-bul · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Delectable is highly delightful, especially to the senses -- a real treat to taste or savor.

Even the pickiest eater at the potluck went back for a second helping of the delectable mushroom risotto.

Example

Food critics rarely agree on anything, but every single review of the new bistro called its slow-roasted lamb utterly delectable.

Delectable most often describes food, praising it as intensely enjoyable to taste, though it can occasionally describe other delightful sensory experiences too.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

scrumptious: Scrumptious is a playful, informal word for delightfully tasty food -- the word you might use grinning over a warm cookie. Delectable praises the same delight in a more elevated, appreciative register, the word a food critic might reach for. Both insist the food truly delights.

delicious: Delicious is the plain, everyday word for food that tastes very good. Delectable makes a stronger claim of delight -- it presents the food as a treat to savor, a notch above merely tasting good, and it carries a more elevated, appreciative tone.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

unpalatable: unpleasant to taste

revolting: causing intense disgust

Where it sits · how strongly it tempts the senses

tasty → delectable → irresistible

tasty vs. delectable: Tasty just means pleasant to eat -- it doesn't carry quite the same intensity of delight as delectable.

irresistible vs. delectable: Irresistible goes even further than delectable, describing something so appealing that turning it down feels impossible.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — delect-: to delight, to charm (Latin delectare)

suffix — -able: able to; tending to (Latin -abilis)

Put it together: Delectable comes from Latin delectare ('to delight, to charm'), a close cousin of the everyday word delight itself. Something delectable is, at root, something able to delight -- most often the senses of taste and smell.

Use the root in a new word: delight: Half the delight of the trip, Dad insists, is planning the route.

Word Choice

Delectable is almost always about food or drink -- reach for it when 'delicious' feels too plain and you want a slightly more elevated, appreciative word.
